security_audit.summary: The static command and reconnaissance matches are mostly false positives caused by markdown references and incident-response terminology. I found a separate medium-risk operational safety issue: the skill asks agents to implement mitigations and emergency deployments without explicit approval gates.

remediation.issue: Production-changing incident actions lack explicit authorization gates.
remediation.suggestion: Require human approval before traffic rerouting, feature flag changes, scaling actions, production fixes, or emergency deployments.

content.value_statement: Production incidents need fast triage, clear ownership, and reliable communication under pressure. This skill structures response across severity classification, observability review, mitigation, deployment, stakeholder updates, and postmortems.
actual_capabilities: Classifies incidents into P0 through P3 severity levels based on impact.
Coordinates observability review across tracing, metrics, logs, APM, and real user monitoring.
Guides immediate mitigation planning, including rollback assessment and feature flag decisions.
Structures root cause analysis across debugging, security, and performance perspectives.
Creates stakeholder communication, customer impact, postmortem, and prevention workflows.
limitations: It does not connect to monitoring, paging, deployment, or ticketing systems by itself.
It depends on accurate incident context, logs, alerts, and service ownership data from the user.
It should not make production changes without explicit human approval.
The referenced implementation playbook is not included in the scanned file structure.

use_cases.title: Triage a Production Outage
use_cases.description: Classify severity, identify affected services, assign incident roles, and plan the first mitigation steps.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Incident Communications
use_cases.description: Prepare status updates, internal summaries, executive notes, and support briefings during an active incident.

use_cases.title: Run a Blameless Postmortem
use_cases.description: Build a timeline, document root cause, define owners, and convert lessons into prevention work.

prompt_templates.title: Classify an Incident
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner triage for a new alert.
prompt_templates.prompt: Classify this incident using the P0 through P3 scale. Include affected services, user impact, business risk, and immediate owner roles: [incident details].

prompt_templates.title: Plan the First Response
prompt_templates.scenario: Structured response after severity is known.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a first-hour incident response plan for this severity and service impact. Include investigation steps, mitigation options, communication cadence, and validation checks: [incident details].

prompt_templates.title: Investigate Root Cause
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this incident with observability, debugging, security, and performance perspectives. Identify likely root cause, contributing factors, evidence gaps, and next actions: [incident evidence].

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Recovery and Postmortem
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a recovery, validation, communication, and postmortem plan for this incident. Include rollback readiness, customer impact, action items, owners, and prevention work: [incident timeline].

output_examples.input: A checkout service has high latency, increased failed payments, and recent deployment activity.
output_examples.output: The response identifies a likely P1 incident, assigns incident command roles, recommends rollback assessment, requests payment error logs, and drafts customer support talking points.

output_examples.input: A security alert shows unusual authentication failures and possible data exposure.
output_examples.output: The response prioritizes containment, audit log review, access pattern analysis, customer impact tracking, legal escalation, and a clear status update cadence.

output_examples.input: The incident is resolved and the team needs a postmortem.
output_examples.output: The response creates a timeline, root cause summary, contributing factors, action items with owners, monitoring improvements, and follow-up deadlines.

best_practices: Confirm severity, user impact, and incident commander before starting parallel work.
Keep mitigation, communication, and evidence collection active throughout the incident.
Require approval and rollback readiness before any production-changing action.
anti_patterns: Do not skip stakeholder updates while engineers investigate technical details.
Do not deploy emergency fixes without validation criteria and rollback triggers.
Do not assign blame in the postmortem or omit contributing system factors.

faq.question: Does this skill replace an incident commander?
faq.answer: No. It supports the incident commander with structure, prompts, and checklists, but humans own decisions and approvals.

faq.question: Can it query monitoring tools directly?
faq.answer: No. It can guide what to inspect, but users must provide tool access, logs, dashboards, or exported evidence.

faq.question: Which incident severities does it support?
faq.answer: It defines P0 through P3 levels, from complete outage or breach to minor or cosmetic issues.

faq.question: Can it help with security incidents?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes steps for DDoS indicators, access failures, data exposure risks, certificates, and suspicious access patterns.

faq.question: What should users provide for best results?
faq.answer: Provide alert details, affected services, recent changes, logs, metrics, customer impact, and any current mitigation status.

faq.question: Does it create postmortem material?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides timelines, root cause analysis, action items, owners, monitoring improvements, and prevention planning.
